Hello fellow kids. I just bought my first road bike and was wondering what kind of pedals do you guys recommend i use? It came with the plastic demo pedals installed. I will use this bike to lessen my status as a fat ass.

depends how much you are thinking of spending and what you're looking to do.

if you're new to bikes and want to see how you adjust first, i'd recommend some toe clips. Pretty cheap on the Amazon but your local target, REI, Sports Authority, whatever should have them also them too at usually the same price.

with these, you just attach them to the pedals you've already got and you get the 'push and pull' peddling experience without having to buy some clips and shoes. since you can use your regular shoes, this also gives you the option of using your bike as a commuter bike without having to always bring extra shoes.

if you're looking to go clipless, the shimano spd, like this, is pretty standard. provides a lot of options on shoes too so you can get a deal.

hope this helps but i am happy to go into more shoe details and recommendations if you want. happy riding!
Thanks for the reply. My bike's pedals came with toe clips installed but I'm not used to them. I'l just have to try them out.

they definitely take some getting used to. the benefit is if for some reason you can't get in right away after a stop or something, the pedals are still large enough to pedal normally so you can get out of traffic or whatever. the other benefit is they are a lot easier to get out of (till you're used to them anyway) compared with clipless. much lower chance of falling over because you can't click out that way.
That was my fear with using them. Getting in and out of them without falling over at a stop.

Right now I run Keo Look Plus pedals and cleats on my road bike, which have been great, and I'd highly recommend them. They're moderately light, nice and stiff, and very smooth, everything you want in a good road pedal. Obviously there are 'better' pedals out there, but those are generally made out of carbon composites, titanium, etc. and are several times the price.

Also, no matter what system you end up going with, remember to grease the threads on your new pedals before installing them. Your future self will thank you.

I'd stick with the normal pedals that came on the bike. Messing with straps or special cleats isn't necessary. They're supposed to give you a more efficient pedal stroke, but check this out:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CNedIJBZpgM

Honestly, I think you're better off just wearing normal shoes and sticking to flats for now anyway. Even if straps or clipless pedals turn out to still be better, you're probably not ready for them at this stage. Get used to the bike first, and get confident riding with traffic. Then you can try out the goofy shit that makes you fall down.

I went from flat pedals to SPDs back when I had a hybrid then upgraded to a road bike and to SPD-SLs. I really liked the security of being clipped in and the ability to be able to pull up when sprinting/starting a climb. It seems like a big jump but for me it was no going back once I tried it!

Dont see how you all do it

Beards itch for two reasons. First, when you first start growing a beard after having shaved all your life, your beard hairs are sliced off, leaving a sharp edge on the hair. If you shaved really close to the skin, then the beard hair can sometimes get sucked back into the follicle. This means that as it grows, it scrapes the edges of the follicle as it comes back out, causing itch.

Second, if you have a full-grown and manly beard, but it itches, this is due to a combination of dry skin and a wiry, scraggly beard. If your beard is not moisturized or conditioned, it will get dry, brittle, and coarse. During the course of a day, it will rub against your cheeks and chin, causing irritation and itch.

Clean and condition. Moisturize with beard oil or balm. If that fails, there are actual anti beard itching shampoos and oils.

http://www.amazon.com/exec/obidos/ASIN/B00IIS6GAO/growabeard-20

A beard is a beard, big or small.

This right here is a smoking gun.

It's not even remotely a long leap to assume that they did it under the guise of Brady.

Quotes from Brady himself:

"I didn't alter the ball in any way," Brady said. "I have a process that I go through before every game where I pick the balls that I want to use for the game. ... "I read that," Brady conceded. "I said that and I like them at 12.5 PSI (which is within the limits set forth by the league). To me, that's a perfect grip for the football. I think that particular term -- deflated or inflated, whatever norm you're using -- I would never do anything outside of the rules of play."

From here we find that:

Brady said he learned those balls had been inflated to 16 pounds per square inch (PSI), which prompted him to look up the rule for air-pressure limits.

He found out the range was from 12.5 to 13.5 PSI, and he told Patriots equipment manager Dave Schoenfeld to "make sure when the referees get the balls, give them this sheet of paper that highlighted" the minimum and the maximum. Brady specifically said at that time that the balls should be inflated to 12.5 PSI.

You cannot claim that the balls might have been deflated but if they had, that Brady had no knowledge of his ballboy's actions in deflating or inflating the footballs to a specific pressure. Brady is on record that he likes his balls at a very specific PSI and that the Jets game caused him to be very vigilant on making sure that the balls were not going to be 16 PSI again.
